chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Samman al-Armani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the fasting one sees a group of people eating, or a man eating, every hair of his supplicates for him.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a fasting person's body when they see others eating?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the heightened spiritual sensitivity of the fasting believer, where the physical state of the body becomes a vehicle for divine supplication. This concept of 'hair supplicating' reflects the Shia understanding of the body as an instrument of worship, where even inanimate parts participate in the spiritual struggle against desire. It underscores the merit of fasting not merely as abstention, but as an active state of devotion that engages the entire being in remembrance of God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al samman Al Armany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the Fasting-one sees a group of people eating, or a man eating, every hair of his supplicates for him’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Samman al-Armaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
when a fasting person observes people or a person eating food, every piece of his hair feels a kind of covering (tranquility).”
